key_insight: Astropauses are most likely to co-locate when the flow stagnation point and magnetic null arise from a pressure extremum with a non-singular local field structure; otherwise, they can separate only under special non-ideal conditions.
engineering_relevance: This clarifies when hydropause and magnetopause can be treated as the same boundary in stellar-wind/interstellar-medium models, simplifying boundary detection and plasma-physics simulations.
method: Analyzed stationary counterstreaming ideal hydrodynamic flows with non-monotonous pressure.
Extended the proof to ideal MHD using momentum-equation quasi-linearity and Jacobian rank arguments.
Generalized to resistive and non-ideal MHD by checking when curl terms force co-located nulls.
evidence_signal: The paper provides analytical proofs and condition-based derivations rather than a numerical dataset, showing co-location under specified regularity, non-degeneracy, and Jacobian conditions.
watch_item: Co-location is not guaranteed in fully non-ideal systems; implementation must verify the curl structure of non-ideal terms and local Jacobian singularity/non-singularity.
paper_title: The existence of null points of flow and magnetic fields as prerequisites for the presence of astropauses and their co-location
